explanation:
Independent production reconstruction complete; no approved ledger, implementation rationale, or agent history was inspected. No patch-introduced defect meeting the evidence threshold was established in this cluster; the observations below distinguish actual behavior and structural risks from asserted bugs. No builds, tests, linters, formatters, or runtime validation were run.

OWNERSHIP AND INTERFACES
• src/languages/module_resolver.rs:53–71,121–234 owns language policy declarations: crate-private SourcePathIdentity::{Logical,Physical}, the crate-private Send+Sync ModuleResolver trait, and get_module_resolver(Language) -> &'static dyn ModuleResolver. The dispatch exhaustively maps Rust and CSharp. ModuleContext carries current_file, the complete borrowed DiscoverySnapshot, a once-per-file optional anchor, and optional NamespaceMap. The snapshot is broader than the resolver currently consumes: Rust reads discovery.crates; C# reads namespaces, not evaluated projects/units.
• RustModuleResolver (module_resolver.rs:265–348) declares Logical identity and '::' import storage, calculates its source-root anchor via rust_src_root_for, delegates path probing to public resolver::resolve_module_path, and itself owns longest-prefix-first qualified candidate enumeration, including implicit-crate-before-as-written precedence and within-split deduplication. It is therefore not merely a pass-through adapter. rust_src_root_for (240–256) asks cargo::get_crate_for_file and falls back with a debug message to file.parent(), then workspace_root.
• CSharpModuleResolver (module_resolver.rs:360–434) declares Physical identity and '.' imports. It intentionally declines single-file segment resolution and qualified_splits; resolve_import_files clones the namespace map's matching vector. Missing namespace context/key yields an empty vector. Its glob policy is UniqueAcrossAll, type kinds Class/Struct/Interface/Enum, callable static-member kinds Function/Method. Static-member detection splits at the final dot and returns the namespace's files plus the suffix type name. Qualified symbol/reference storage remains canonical '::', separate from import formatting.
• src/indexing.rs:1200–1279 owns actual source selection, rather than the resolver trait: crate-private discover_files takes indexed-path iterator and mutable skipped-directory/error sinks and returns Result<(Vec<(PathBuf,Language)>,usize)>. It combines walk results, retained existing indexed paths, then evaluated unit source paths; applies the resolver's identity choice; deduplicates; and selects the final parser language. The automatic walker and exclusion policy remain in the same protected parent (1285–1350).
• src/lib.rs:294–345 owns query identity execution through crate-private relative_path(&Path) -> Cow<Path>. Public get_file, list_symbols, reference/import queries, dependency/dependent queries, dependency paths and changed-file consumers route through it. The resolver declares identity, but filesystem canonicalization, containment and fallback mechanics are independently implemented here and in indexing.rs.
• src/reindex.rs:66–154 owns freshness orchestration over the shared selector; lookup_key (235–238) adapts relative_path into db::normalize_path. classify_indexed_file (316–338) owns shared mtime/size classification. update and rebuild are actual thin adapters to indexing; needs_update/get_stale_files are substantive drivers, not pass-through wrappers. src/unused_imports.rs:92–183 owns Rust-only live-disk analysis, calls the same selector, filters the returned Language::Rust tag, parallel-parses and textually rereads inputs, then queries the DB only for confidence upgrades.

DEPENDENCY DIRECTION AND CONCRETE ADAPTERS
• Tethys::open_workspace (lib.rs:183–220) canonicalizes the workspace root and loads persisted discovery; if absent, it creates a default snapshot with Cargo discovery only. It does not invoke MSBuild discovery. Tethys stores Arc<DiscoverySnapshot>.
• index_in_revision (indexing.rs:181–201) starts the DB revision, constructs DiscoveryRequest with options and DB cache, calls discover_workspace, installs the new Arc snapshot, runs indexing and commits. DiscoveryRun restores the previous in-memory snapshot on an unsuccessful run. index_discovered_revision (218–237) adapts DB IndexedFile paths to source selection. The public discovery module's discover_workspace (src/discovery/mod.rs:36–41) calls concrete CargoDiscovery and MsBuildDiscovery adapters and composes the latter snapshot with Cargo crates; it contains no source-query normalization.
• Public SourceMembership (discovery/types.rs:365–372) represents canonical workspace-relative physical source path plus optional Link metadata; EvaluationUnit.sources (396–410) allows membership in multiple units. DiscoveryRequest validates/canonicalizes its system-boundary root (169 onward). The source selector consumes membership.path, not Link, framework, properties or references, so source syntax is indexed once independently of unit participation.
• parse_file_static (indexing.rs:664–788) is the tuple-to-parser adapter: it reads bytes, rejects invalid UTF-8, chooses LanguageSupport from the supplied language, extracts symbols/imports/references, and emits ParsedFileData with a strip_prefix-derived relative path. It does not independently canonicalize: logical Rust paths remain logical. Read/metadata/parser failures propagate; unusable timestamps log and publish 0. Qualified symbol names use '::'.
• Consumers of resolver-produced control values were inspected: resolve.rs:352–388 explicitly dispatches both GlobPolicy variants, with deliberate decline for qualified C# references; resolve.rs:467–490 consumes QualifiedSplit files in order, lets the first indexed file claim a split, and abandons remaining candidates on a tail miss. SourcePathIdentity is explicitly consumed in discover_files (1236–1255) and tested in relative_path (295–301). No unhandled new identity variant or dropped candidate payload was found.

IDENTITY, ERROR AND FALLBACK INVARIANTS
• Rust walk paths retain workspace-relative aliases, including links to external targets; separate logical names can produce distinct file/symbol rows. C# candidates canonicalize and must remain under the canonical workspace root. A physical candidate that fails canonicalization or escapes emits warn! and an IoError into the caller's sink, then is skipped (indexing.rs:1238–1254).
• Selection is union-based, not Compile-membership filtering: walked sources remain eligible without confirmed projects, evaluated sources bypass walk exclusions, and previously indexed existing sources are retained after participation disappears. The retention loop itself applies to every indexed language, not just physical sources (1209–1213); its comments should not be mistaken for a language filter.
• Physical queries canonicalize workspace-root-relative inputs, accept the resulting contained target, and otherwise fall back to lexical/original lookup (lib.rs:312–345). Missing files therefore remain addressable by stored physical spelling. An alias whose target no longer exists cannot be reverse-mapped to its former canonical row. Absolute outside-workspace input is returned as-is with debug logging; this helper is lookup normalization, not an authorization/error-return API. Logical in-workspace inputs take the lexical path before any filesystem access.
• lexically_normalize (lib.rs:132–157) removes dot segments and collapses intra-path parents, but returns the original input for upward escape or absolute/prefix components. It does not resolve symlink-plus-parent semantics. db::normalize_path (db/files.rs:44 onward) converts the path to a lossy string and changes backslashes only on Windows; this is distinct from source identity.
• Freshness source diagnostics and skipped directories are collected but not exposed in needs_update/get_stale_files (reindex.rs:69–78,119–128), and unused-import analysis likewise does not return source-selection diagnostics (unused_imports.rs:92–100). Warnings are emitted at the selector. Source rows absent from selection become deleted in the report; metadata NotFound also means Deleted, other metadata failures mean Modified, and unavailable/pre-epoch freshness timestamps use i64::MIN rather than the indexer's 0. These are concrete error contracts, not claims that new APIs must change them.
• Read-only freshness/unused-import queries consume the loaded snapshot and filesystem; they do not call discover_workspace or execute project evaluation. Consequently freshness answers source-byte/mtime/size questions, not whether current project configuration would produce different membership.

PATH-SHAPE AND ORDERING OBSERVATIONS
• Language is detected twice during selection (indexing.rs:1228–1235 and1261–1269), once before identity normalization and once afterward. Thus Alias.cs pointing to target.rs is selected using physical policy but parsed as Rust; Alias.cs pointing to an unsupported-extension target is skipped; Alias.rs pointing to Target.cs retains logical spelling and parses as Rust. Query policy is selected from the query spelling's extension. These are verified control-flow consequences and useful cross-language fences, not asserted regressions without a required contract.
• The seen HashSet is membership-only; output is appended in first-encounter order (1256–1272), not iterated from the set. There is no new explicit sort. The walker inherits read_dir order; retained-only candidates in freshness inherit HashMap key iteration; deleted results also inherit HashMap order (reindex.rs:146). Do not describe discovery/freshness output as globally deterministic. Existing resolver candidate priority is explicit, and unused-import output explicitly sorts by file/line/name (unused_imports.rs:161–164).

PROTECTED-PARENT GROWTH RISKS
• indexing.rs now contains source union, existence probing, identity normalization, containment, deduplication, parser-language inference and diagnostic construction in addition to indexing orchestration and walking. lib.rs separately implements related identity mechanics. The central resolver policy enum avoids hard-coded language switches but does not yet centralize these mechanisms; future path-policy changes can drift across both parents.
• ModuleContext's dependency on the whole discovery snapshot couples the existing resolution seam to discovery representation despite only needing crates today. Conversely discover_files reaches into snapshot.units.sources directly, so participation-to-source adaptation is owned by the indexing parent rather than an encapsulated source-selection interface. These are structural facts/risks for Main's later comparison, not standalone correctness findings.

TEST SURFACES READ, NOT EXECUTED
• tests/symlink_boundary.rs exercises public Tethys indexing/query APIs. Strengthened external Rust file/directory tests assert logical file rows and symbols (26–122); the in-workspace alias test asserts two distinct file and symbol identities (265–336). Circular-link and chain cases retain looser assertions and rely on OS termination; dangling symlinks remain silently absent.
• tests/concurrency_and_filesystem.rs:272–340 checks readable-source publication and typed incomplete discovery when a directory is inaccessible, with an elevated-user skip. Its C# identity test (432–515) checks one physical row and symbol across relative/absolute/file/directory/dotted aliases, dependency queries, and no freshness change. The external C# alias test (519–553 onward) checks nonpublication and query misses. These tests use public APIs rather than calling discover_files/relative_path internals.
• tests/msbuild_discovery.rs uses real native options and direct SQLite observers. Native/worker-dependent tests are ignored by default. membership_replacement (175–276) asserts multiple-unit membership with single syntax rows, project replacement, persisted snapshot reopening and membership surviving a failed syntax parse with null file association. bounded_failures_replace_confirmed_units (280–379) checks partial/outer failure replacement. untrusted_publication_retains_source_only_facts (382–420) is nonignored and checks source syntax without evaluated membership. evaluated_only_sources_share_publication_and_freshness_identity (424–452) checks excluded-directory evaluated sources, reopening, later modification, retained syntax after project removal, and source deletion.
• These discovery integration tests reach through the storage boundary: observer, membership and strings (61–92) query concrete table names, joins, standing_json and nullable file_id directly. That is stronger persistence evidence but couples the tests to schema representation. No test in the inspected files fences cross-extension aliases, missing physical-alias reverse lookup, or retention-order stability; no validation result is claimed.
